title: Customer status lifecycle and oncall fallback procedures
content:
Purpose: This working draft defines the lifecycle for customer-facing status messages and the on-call fallback procedures used when primary responders are unavailable. Focused on clarity, minimal exposure time, and predictable escalation so product teams and customers see timely, accurate signals during incidents.

Context and goals:
- Provide a short, repeatable set of templates for status page updates and customer-facing emails.
- Make internal war-room checklist operational and easy for a bridge lead or deputy to run through under pressure.
- Document explicit fallback steps if the on-call owner is unreachable (who calls whom, how quickly, and where to post).
- Keep language vendor-neutral and measurable (no jargon that confuses customers).

Audience:
- SREs who will run the bridge and author status updates.
- Support and Customer Success engineers who need copy to send to customers.
- Product and Sales stakeholders who require timing/cadence for updates.

Quick summary (one-line):
If outages impact customer-facing inference or control-plane operations, start with the status page Investigation post within first 10 minutes; escalate to Identified within 30–60 minutes when scope is known; publish Monitoring and Resolved updates per the cadence below.

Incident lifecycle and timing expectations:
- 0–10 minutes: Triage & open bridge. Post status: "Investigating" (minimal facts). Internal: create incident doc (INC-{{id}}), open Slack #incident-bridge-{{id}}.
- 10–30 minutes: Rapid data collection (scope, impact vector, affected models/regions). If customer-visible degradation is confirmed, prepare customer-facing note.
- 30–60 minutes: Post status: "Identified" with root-cause hypothesis and ETA for next update. If customer impact is broad or SLA-affecting, CS should be notified using the template below.
- 60+ minutes: Update cadence every 60 minutes by default until Monitoring/Resolved. Shorter cadence if severity escalates.

Status page templates (short, single-paragraph entries for the status-system):
- Investigating (initial)
  Title: Investigating: Elevated error rates for inference requests in region(s) {{region}}
  Body: We are investigating elevated error rates affecting inference requests in {{region}}. Users may experience increased latency or failed requests. Our engineers are actively triaging. Incident ID: INC-{{id}}. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.

- Identified
  Title: Identified: Upstream GPU provisioning bug causing request failures
  Body: We have identified a cause affecting inference throughput in {{region}} linked to a GPU provisioning path. A subset of requests are failing or timing out. Workarounds in progress; mitigation steps are being applied. Estimated time to partial mitigation: ~{{eta_minutes}} minutes.

- Monitoring
  Title: Monitoring: Mitigation applied, monitoring for recurrence
  Body: We have applied mitigation steps and are monitoring the system for recurrence. Error rates have decreased and latency is returning to baseline for most customers. If you continue to see problems, contact support.

- Resolved
  Title: Resolved: Service restored to baseline
  Body: The root cause has been fixed and the service is operating normally. We are conducting post-incident analysis and will follow up with a summary soon. If you see residual issues, please open a support ticket.

Customer-facing email templates (concise, enterprise-focused):
- Short alert (when impact confirmed, for account owners)
  Subject: Incident {{id}} — Degraded inference performance in {{region}}
  Body: Hi {{customer_name}},

  We are currently observing degraded inference performance for workloads in {{region}}. Our engineers have identified the issue and are actively working on mitigation. We will send updates every {{cadence_minutes}} minutes and post public updates at https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-{{id}}.

  Estimated time to partial mitigation: {{eta_minutes}} minutes.

  If you have critical SLO concerns, please reply and we will escalate directly to our account response team.

  — Priya (SRE Lead)

- Detailed follow-up (post-mitigation, pre-postmortem)
  Subject: Incident {{id}} — Update and temporary workarounds
  Body: Hi {{customer_name}},

  We implemented a mitigation that restored service for most traffic. For persistent issues, please try a short retry with exponential backoff, or route traffic to an alternate region if possible. We will share the full post-incident summary by {{postmortem_date}}.

  Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience.

  Best,
  Redwood Inference SRE

Notes on tone and content: keep it factual, avoid speculation, and show ownership. Always link to the public status page for canonical updates.

Internal war-room checklist (use as a daily checklist inside the incident doc):
- Bridge lead assigned (Name / Slack handle)
- Incident doc created and pinned in Slack/bridge channel
- Triage summary posted to channel within 10 minutes (impact, likely scope, affected services)
- Primary mitigation hypothesis and immediate action (e.g., scale pool, rollback, config flip)
- Customer success notified if >1% of customers or any large customer affected
- Legal/Comms briefed for SEV1s (if required)
- Decide escalation to on-call infra or platform team; open associated tickets
- Post status page Investigating/Identified/Monitoring updates on schedule
- Track time-to-mitigation and time-to-resolution as metrics in doc
- After stabilization, schedule postmortem and assign owner for follow-up tasks

On-call fallback and unreachable primary flow (explicit steps):
1) If primary on-call does not acknowledge within 7 minutes after bridge creation, the deputy (first listed on rota) takes bridge lead. Post in #oncall-escalation and ping the oncall-deputy group.
2) If deputy is unreachable after 10 minutes, escalate to the SRE pager escalation list (SMS and phone).
3) If nobody from SRE is reachable within 20 minutes, contact cross-functional backup (platform-eng lead, infra manager).
4) If customer-impacting and >30 minutes with no lead, Customer Success Director is notified and sales has the right to proactively contact top affected customers.

Practical keys: always post a short status update to the bridge channel when changing leadership ("Bridge lead change: Priya -> Miguel at 2025-11-04T15:23Z — reason: unreachable"). Keep a running timeline in the incident doc and mark the leader transitions.

Stakeholder matrix (who to notify depending on severity):
- SEV1 (complete outage or large SLA breach): CTO, Head of SRE, Head of Product, Customer Success Director, Legal
- SEV2 (major degradation for many customers): Head of SRE, Product PM, Affected Account Managers, Support Lead
- SEV3 (partial, non-critical): On-call SRE, Support, CS for escalations

Channel guidance and snippets:
- Slack: #incident-bridge-{{id}} (use clear subject and pin incident doc). Use threads for customer-specific notes.
- Pager duty: attach incident doc link and short triage note.
- Dedicated zoom/meet link: required for SEV1/SEV2 centralized coordination.

Examples of quick Slack snippets (copy-paste):
- "Investigating: elevated 5xx for inference in eu-west-1. Triage started. INC-{{id}}. Lead: @priyash. ETA next update 30m."
- "Identified: provisioning race in GPU pool controller. Mitigation: scale-down then drain affected hosts. ETA 45m. @miguel please own scaling."

Post-incident and audit items (immediately after Resolution):
- Confirm status page shows Resolved and then archive after 72 hours.
- Open postmortem doc, assign author within 48 hours.
- Runbook updates: if the incident required manual steps not in existing runbooks, add a runbook PR and request review.
- Customer follow-ups: ensure account-level emails have been sent for affected customers and a CS owner assigned.
- Metrics capture: capture error-rate curves, time to mitigation, and any cost/credit implications for billing adjustments.

Open questions / draft decisions to resolve before marking final:
- Default customer update cadence (30 vs 60 minutes) depending on severity. Current draft uses 60m for SEV2, 30m for SEV1.
- Exact phone/SMS escalation list and contact ownership for international holidays.

References and useful links:
- Confluence bridge playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-bridge-playbook
- PagerDuty escalation docs: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/esc

Revision log:
- 2025-07-21: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-08-05: added customer templates and stakeholder matrix (Miguel)
- 2026-01-18: refined fallback timings and added audit checklist (Leah)

End of doc.
